title: Does higher accuracy mean a better classifier?
description: Course activity for Exercise 10: compares ordinary logistic regression against logistic regression with class_weight="balanced" across five progressively more imbalanced control:autism samples (50:50 through 90:10), all at a fixed decision threshold of 0.5.
instructions: Choose a control:autism class balance. Both models below always use the same participants, the same training/test split, and the same 0.5 decision threshold -- only the sample's class balance changes. Raw accuracy can rise simply because the majority class becomes easier to guess as it grows, and the majority-class baseline itself rises with it. Class weighting can improve autism recall, balanced accuracy, or F1, but it does not improve every metric at every balance -- compare the numbers directly rather than assuming one model is simply better.
reflectionPrompts: As control participants become more common, does higher accuracy necessarily mean a better classifier?
How far is each model's accuracy above the majority-class baseline at each balance?
Which model detects more autistic participants, and does that answer change across balances?
Which conclusion changes when you look at recall, F1, or PR-AUC instead of accuracy alone?
